links.comparator_used: LLM given the case images alone (raw images, no free-text descriptions)
links.effect: 52.7% with images vs 63.9% with reader-generated descriptions; descriptions from thoracic radiologists gave 67.3% vs 60.4% from residents (p < .001)
links.tradeoff: Benefit depended on reader expertise, since resident-written descriptions gave lower LLM accuracy than thoracic radiologist descriptions.
links.quote: LLM accuracy was 52.7% when images were inputted and 63.9% when reader-generated descriptions were inputted.

links.comparator_used: Reader's own initial interpretation without LLM output (session 1 vs session 2)
links.effect: Thoracic radiologists 56.3% to 65.6%; residents 42.4% to 58.5%; gain greater for residents (16.1 vs 9.2 percentage points; p = .02)
links.tradeoff: New failure mode: residents accepted LLM-favored diagnoses more often than thoracic radiologists (73.2% vs 48.9%; p < .001). They also switched to an incorrect diagnosis more often after misleading LLM output (60.6% vs 32.4%; p = .009).
links.quote: From session 1 to session 2, accuracy increased from 56.3% to 65.6% for thoracic radiologists and from 42.4% to 58.5% for residents, respectively.

design_hint: human-in-the-loop reader review of LLM output
